preconditions.description: The number of lamps n is an integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n - 1 and all(1 <= x <= n for x in a)
preconditions.description: The input list a has exactly n-1 elements, each between 1 and n inclusive, representing the main lamp indices for each wire in descending order of importance.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (stdout.split() and (k := int(stdout.split()[0])) in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: If no valid scheme exists, output is '-1'. Otherwise, the first line of output is an integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ n), the index of the lamp connected to the power grid.
If a valid scheme exists, the output consists of k followed by exactly n-1 pairs of lamp indices (x_i, y_i), each pair representing a wire connecting two distinct lamps.

postconditions.expression: stdout != '-1' and all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= n and int(x) != int(y) for line in stdout.split()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: All lamp indices in the output are valid (1 ≤ x_i, y_i ≤ n) and distinct for each wire.

postconditions.expression: stdout != '-1' and (k := int(stdout.split()[0])) and (wires := [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.split()[1:]]) and (is_valid_scheme(n, k, wires, a))
postconditions.description: The output scheme (k, wires) must be a valid tree where k is the root (connected to the grid), and the list of main lamp indices for wires, when sorted by descending importance, matches the input list a. The importance of a wire is defined as the sum of brightness values (2^i) of all lamps in the subtree disconnected from the grid if the wire is cut.
